note: Baseline. Real timetable, ordinary maintenance load.
Festival/peak period: additional passenger services on the real paths, squeezing the cheap windows.
Freight surge. Bites hardest at night, which is where much maintenance wants to go.
Accumulated backlog after blocks were refused. This is the scenario in which the reliability constraint actually binds.
Poorly characterised work. Tests whether the planner trades bundle size for hand-back reliability.
A quarter of the cheap windows are withdrawn mid-horizon, forcing a re-plan. Used for the plan-stability metric.

Higher maintenance demand across all three departments on the same real sections, so cross-department bundling has more to gain. The mix is whatever the periodicity-and-asset-inventory arrival model produces at this rate; it is NOT force-balanced between ENGG/SNT/TRD, and must not be described as such.
